title: The explicit K-flat quotient tensor comparison commutes with one successor
statement: Let X be a scheme, A a commutative ring, J an ideal, U an object of the coefficient-sized pro-etale site, and R the completed coefficient sheaf on U. Let P be a K-flat R-module-sheaf complex, M an object of D(R), and eP:Q(P)≅M. Use the actual quotient tensor tower T(P) of [def-sfb-adic-residue-quotient-tensor-tower] and the normalized scalar-adjoint tower G(M) of [lem-sfb-adic-residue-adjoint-tower]. Define c_n:Q(T(P)_n)≅G(M)_n explicitly by Q of the ordinary comparison [lem-sfb-ringed-scalar-tensor-comparison], resFactors, the inverse universal scalar comparison on P, and restriction of scalar extension of eP. Then for every n the equality Q(T(P)_(n+1)→T(P)_n) followed by c_n.hom equals c_(n+1).hom followed by adicResidueAdjointStep(M,n). This is one specified successor square and contains neither an existence assertion for an isomorphism of towers nor a unit assertion.

source.place: Section tensor-product (03EK), the sheafified tensor formulas; lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict (03CZ), scalar adjunction. For derived comparisons: sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-derived-base-change (06YY). For quotient transitions: proetale.tex, lemma-naive-completion (099M).

proof.text: Use scalarTensorModuleIso_pure and the naturality of the degree-zero totalization contraction to compare the actual quotient tensor successor with the canonical ordinary scalarTransition. Cancel the level isomorphisms and test on the scalar-extension pure tensors; both maps replace s by its image in the next quotient.

Prove that ordinary balancing preserves insertion of one by its specified pure-tensor formula. For each normalized derived scalar adjunction, its Hom equivalence on a K-flat source is represented by the ordinary Hom equivalence, followed by resFactors. Apply this twice: scalar extension preserves K-flatness, and the exact-restriction compositor respects resFactors. The resulting equation is precisely the normalization defining adicFiniteExtendComp. Its uniqueness identifies this comparison with the left-adjoint-uniqueness comparison of the composed adjunction.

Use the identified adjoint-uniqueness comparison to compute the transpose of the reduced preceding counit. The triangle identity cancels that counit with its unit, leaving scalar insertion for the quotient map, followed by exact restriction composition and derived balancing. Independently factor ordinary scalarTransition by ordinary insertion, restriction composition and ordinary balancing; the defining K-flat computation equations identify its localization with the same derived composite.

The composite of scalar insertion, exact restriction composition and derived balancing is natural in the input derived object. Transport the previous identity along eP, specialize f and g to the completed-ring projection and actual quotient successor, and combine with the ordinary tensor successor square from step 1. These composites are exactly the specified level isomorphisms and adicResidueAdjointStep.

lean.statement:
theorem adicResidueQuotientTensorLevelIso_successor
    (P : Cx ((completed (coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X) A J).over U))
    (hP : P.IsAcyclicTensorKFlat) (M : AdicResidueLocalDerived.{u, v} X J U)
    (eP : (Q _).obj P ≅ M) (n : ℕ) :
    (Q _).map ((adicResidueQuotientTensorTower X J U P).map
        (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) ≫
      (adicResidueQuotientTensorLevelIso X J U P hP M eP n).hom =
    (adicResidueQuotientTensorLevelIso X J U P hP M eP (n + 1)).hom ≫
      adicResidueAdjointStep.{u, v} X J U M n
